excluded_from_the_population.why: docs/receipts/artifacts/d1-identity.json already binds those base-D1 sample ids to the FINAL user turn (data.audio2tool._entry_media reads chat_history[-1]); contracts.gate_media_identity refuses a D1 supplement that duplicates a base D1 sample and re-hashes the flown file against the base record, so a first-user-turn binding of the same id can never reach the frozen core. The agent-last rows are refused by that same _entry_media, which would break load_official_gold for every Audio2Tool scoring job if one entered a probe-sample receipt. Both exclusions are applied to the POPULATION before the draw and named here.

official_rule_audit.how_the_file_order_rule_resolved: the glob's first element is turn_00_user_*.wav in every one of the 2146 directories; the tier manifest's own chat_history[0] names that same file, with a matching duration, in every one of them, so the released manifest and the released loader agree on the audio this tier evaluates
official_rule_audit.method: replay of audio_benchmark/datasets/tier7_dataset.py::_get_audio_paths at commit b9d5383ca30945fbafb965a04bea40117e1e8a82: sorted(query_dir.glob('turn_*_user_*.wav'))[0], the wav BenchmarkEvaluator evaluates as audio_paths[0] with max_speakers_per_query 1. generation_results.csv is NOT read by this loader, agent turns are not included (include_agent_turns defaults to False) and no history text reaches the prompt
official_rule_audit.note: the released evaluator hears only this first user turn: no chat history, no agent turns and no later user turn reaches the request, while the gold tool call is the one the WHOLE conversation resolves to

population.rule: each tier's released population: for every query_* directory in sorted order, the first recording the released loader resolves. On tiers 3, 4 and 6 that is the shipped speaker with the lowest speaker_idx (the manifest row with the lowest id), exactly as on tiers 1 and 2; on tier 7 the loader ignores generation_results.csv and returns sorted(query_dir.glob('turn_*_user_*.wav')), so audio_paths[0] is the FIRST user turn's wav -- with no chat history and no agent turn in the prompt -- and the tier manifest's own chat_history[0] names that same file with a matching duration on every directory
population.why_not_max_samples: the release orders every subset smart_home -> wearables -> smart_car (its own README), so max_samples 500 over sorted query directories would be a near-pure smart_home sample on all four tiers; each tier's draw below is uniform over its whole population

selection.algorithm: random.Random(seed).sample(population, count_per_tier) per tier, where population is that tier's official first-recording rows in ascending manifest id order (identical to sorted query-directory order); each tier uses its own freshly seeded generator
selection.rule: uniform without replacement over each tier's whole released population

split_identity_hash_convention: sha256 over the LF-joined sorted 'key' values (audio2tool:<tier>:<id6>, UTF-8, no trailing newline) -- the Audio2Tool probe-receipt integrity convention
